newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish govt delays income tax cut until 1998.
newsitem.headline: Polish govt delays income tax cut until 1998.

text.p: Poland will put off a pledged personal and corporate income tax cut until 1998 from the earlier planned 1997, government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said on Tuesday.
Jakubowska told reporters after a cabinet meeting personal income tax levels would stay flat at 21, 33 and 45 percent in 1997 and be reduced to 20, 32 and 44 percent in 1998.
Corporate income tax would be cut by two points to 38 percent in 1998 and be gradually reduced by two points each year to 32 percent by the year 2001.

Jakubowska said the government abandoned plans of lower taxes next year because it needed cash for spending on pensions after the Constitutional Tribunal had ruled the government had to reimburse pensioners for an overdue pension indexation. @

"In view of the ruling of the Constitutional Tribunal on pension indexation and the resulting higher spending needs, the government has accepted the suggestions of parliamentary committees to keep taxes unchanged in 1997," she said.
She said the government also wanted to cut taxes to 20, 30 and 40 percent in 1999.
The tax law will be submitted by the government to the lower house of parliament for its first reading on Wednesday.
